newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SHARES MIXED ON PESSIMISTIC MARKET.
newsitem.headline: SHARES MIXED ON PESSIMISTIC MARKET.

text.p: * Official index down 3.10 points to 897.29 points.
* Group A shares up 12.53 points to 1942.44 points.
* Litin G drops 18 points to 1746.50 points.
* Central market turnover 429,000 litas from 331,000 litas.
* Block trade turnover 570,000 litas from 350,000 litas.
* Market "going nowhere" according to one broker. (A full report follows)
Lithuania's stock market limped through mixed trading Tuesday amid fairly low central market trade and a mood among brokers the market was headed nowhere.
The official list index slipped 3.10 points to 897.29 while group A shares were up 12.53 points to 1942.44. The Litin G index of secondary shares declined 18 points to 1746.50.
Although central market turnover improved to 429,000 litas from 331,000 litas, it was still seen as low.
"Everything is as usual: the market is going nowhere," said Kestutis Kupshys, a broker with Mendes Prior Europe.
"Clients are being very careful now because the market is not active," said Grazhina Bachiuliene, a broker with Vilfima.
"If they buy shares, they buy less than they need...to spread the risk," she added.
Kupshys said supply of shares was far outstripping demand at a ratio of around 13 to one.
Hermis Bank, becoming a favourite stock among brokers, was the most active share, turning over 516,000 litas in block trades at 172 litas.
Hermis turned over 64,000 litas on the central market. Its price on the central market was stable at 180 litas.
"At 180 litas, we see Hermis as undervalued by 10 to 20 percent," Kupshys said.
"We think the price of Hermis might go up a little or at least stay where it is because there is a lot of interest and a lot of clients want to buy Hermis," Bachiuliene said.
